actions.detail: After a stationary set stance holding the ball (0.0-3.6 s, no action), the athlete takes his first approach step at ~3.8-4.0 s (legs separate, body leans in), continues consecutive steps at 4.2-5.2 s, and the approach concludes when the final sliding step finishes into the delivery at ~6.0-6.2 s. Evidence: progressive forward foot travel across frames 4.0-5.4 s ending in the low slide posture at 5.6-6.2 s.

The ball travels rearward from ~4.6 s: it is low and behind the body at 4.8-5.0 s (single-hand grip visible at the right hip), then rises up and behind the head, reaching the rear apex at 5.4 s with the arm extended overhead. Change of direction is marked by the apex frame at 5.4 s.

From the rear apex at 5.4 s the ball swings forward and downward past the body (5.6-5.8 s, ball near the knee/ground beside the slide leg) until hand separation at ~6.0 s. The ball is supported by one hand throughout the swing; no second-hand support is visible.

The final front-foot plant/slide into delivery is observable from ~5.6 s: the body drops low over the planted slide foot while the trailing leg lifts and extends behind (5.8-6.4 s), and the slide posture is held until he begins to rise out of it at ~6.6 s. This overlaps the forward swing and release.

At ~6.0 s the hand ceases to support the ball and it begins independent lane travel: a yellow ball is visible on the lane just past the foul line at 6.0-6.2 s, continuing down the lane at 6.4-6.8 s. Exact finger-separation instant is between the 5.8 s and 6.0 s frames, so timing is approximate.

After release the throwing arm continues its upward/forward path and the body remains low with the trailing leg lifted and extended behind (6.2-7.0 s), then the athlete recovers to an upright stance and starts walking back at ~7.2-7.4 s. Pin impact (~7.6-7.8 s) is excluded as non-technique action.

audio.detail: A brief, sharp click or tap sound.
A loud clattering and scraping noise, like objects being moved or dropped on a hard surface.

caption: After a stationary set stance holding the ball (0.0-3.6 s), the athlete begins his approach at ~3.8 s, taking consecutive steps until the final sliding step concludes into delivery at ~6.2 s. Concurrently, he executes a one-handed backswing starting at ~4.6 s, reaching the rear apex at 5.4 s where a brief sharp click is heard (U001). From this apex, he transitions immediately into a forward swing (5.4-6.0 s) while dropping into a low slide posture with the trailing leg lifted (5.6-6.6 s). He releases the yellow ball at ~6.0 s, which travels down the lane past the foul line. Following the release, he maintains the follow-through position with arm extended and body low until ~7.0 s, then recovers to an upright stance and walks back by 7.4 s. A loud clattering noise occurs from 7.71-8.6 s (U002) as the ball impacts the pins.
